questions.question_text:
Sequence the following sentences in a coherent passage.
P:
This fortuitous geological event generated a colossal amount of energy and
heat that resulted in the rocks rising to an average height of 4 km across the
contact zone.
Q: Thus, the geophysicists tend to think of the Himalayas as an active geological
event rather than as a static geological feature.
R: The natural process of the cooling of this massive edifice absorbed large
quantities of atmospheric carbon dioxide, altering the earth’s atmosphere and
making it better suited for life.
S:
Many millennia ago, a breakaway chunk of bedrock from the Antarctic Plate
collided with the massive Eurasian Plate.
questions.explaination: Sentence S introduces the foundational historical premise (many millennia ago, Antarctic plate collided with Eurasian plate). Sentence P describes the immediate effect of this event (energy/heat rising to 4 km height). Sentence R details the subsequent cooling that altered the atmosphere. Sentence Q concludes with the geophysicists' resulting viewpoint. The logical sequence is SPRQ.

questions.question_text:
A person sold two different items at the same price. He made 10% profit in one
item, and 10% loss in the other item. In selling these two items, the person made a
total of
questions.subtopic: Numerical computation and estimation: ratios, percentages, powers, exponents and logarithms, permutations and combinations, series
questions.explaination: When two items are sold at the same selling price $S$, one at a profit of $x\%$ and the other at a loss of $x\%$, there is always an overall net loss given by $\frac{x^2}{100}\%$. Here $x = 10$, so the net loss is $\frac{10^2}{100}\% = 1\%$ loss.

questions.question_text:
A cube is to be cut into 8 pieces of equal size and shape. Here, each cut should be
straight and it should not stop till it reaches the other end of the cube.
The minimum number of such cuts required is
questions.subtopic: Paper folding, cutting, and patterns in 2 and 3 dimensions
questions.explaination: A single full planar straight cut can at most double the number of pieces. With $k$ cuts through 3 orthogonal dimensions (1 cut parallel to $xy$-plane, 1 parallel to $yz$-plane, 1 parallel to $zx$-plane), the cube is divided into $2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8$ equal pieces. Thus, a minimum of 3 cuts is required.
